attribution.note: Marcus's own first-person words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: 'I'd bet a lot' expresses high confidence, so this is a scored forecast. Saying he would not bet the species only means he is not certain. The drafter's 'likely' modality understates it; under policy, 'likely' would wrongly make it unscorable. The horizon 'now or very soon' is kept.

contract.note: The plain reading of returns as capability gains per added compute or data, with 'diminishing' meaning a real new slowdown, is ordinary and fair. 'Very soon' has no endpoint, and the contract says so.

evidence.note: July 2025 study of sub-scaling mechanisms. It does not show that frontier returns broadly weakened starting around December 2024.
September 2025 study finding that scaling gains depend on the measure used. It is not a longitudinal, resource-normalised comparison, so it neither confirms nor refutes the forecast.

reviews.rationale: This is a high-confidence forecast with no fixed deadline. Neither item is a broad, comparable cross-generation measurement of capability gains per resource. One identifies diminishing-return mechanisms; the other argues the diminishing returns are partly illusory. No conclusive event meets the early-resolution rule, so the outcome is unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own statement in his own post about weaknesses he and Davis identified in 2020.

semantics.note: Faithfully lists the four named areas and the 'not robustly solved' claim as of December 2024. Dropping 'remotely' slightly softens the wording but does not change the commitment.

contract.note: Reading 'robustly solved' as dependable performance across varied, unfamiliar problems, without requiring perfection, is ordinary and fair. A 2024 window up to the post date is reasonable.

evidence.note: May 2024 CaLM study of 28 models finds causal reasoning breaks down as complexity rises. Its model coverage is earlier than December.
February 2024 ContPhy finds state-of-the-art multimodal models struggle with physical reasoning. Early-2024 models and video input limit how far it reaches.
October 2024 SimpleToM: even o1-preview falls short on judging behaviour. Large gains from prompting qualify this, but do not show robustness.
October 2024 GSM-NoOp: irrelevant clauses cause big drops, including for o1-preview, showing mathematical reasoning was not robust.
Strong results on causal tasks, but the study also reports unpredictable errors and prompt sensitivity. It does not show causal reasoning was robustly solved.

reviews.rationale: All four areas show documented, reproducible failures in 2024 evaluations. For psychological and mathematical reasoning these include frontier models such as o1-preview. Coverage of late-2024 models is thinner for causal and physical reasoning, but no item shows dependable performance across any whole area, and the counterevidence (prompting gains, strong causal-task results) does not reach robustness.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Even if' is a concession, not a condition. He firmly states the acceleration 'won't slow down forever', which is an unqualified forecast with no deadline.

contract.note: The contract partly frames this as a conditional, which sits awkwardly with the concessive reading. Its tests are still fair: renewed acceleration after a documented slowdown supports the claim, and no finite period of slowdown can refute 'forever'.

evidence.note: METR (July 2025) reports possibly faster progress in 2024 on time horizons. It shows no slowdown followed by recovery.
METR note (March 2026): time-horizon results are sensitive to analysis choices, which limits inferences about changes in pace.

reviews.rationale: This is an open-ended forecast with no deadline. No measure in the packet establishes a slowdown after the 2019-2023 pace, let alone a later re-acceleration, so the early-resolution rule is not met. 'Forever' cannot be contradicted within a finite window. Unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own statement in his own post. He mentions agreement with Newton but asserts the claim himself.

semantics.note: Accurately captures that, as of the post, there were no guarantees that current or advanced AI would be helpful, harmless and honest. The causal framing 'part of the danger' is reasonably set aside.

contract.note: Reading 'guarantees' as dependable, broad behavioural assurance, not narrow formal proofs, is the ordinary and fair reading. The Q4 2024 window is an evaluator choice but reasonable.

evidence.note: US/UK AISI testing of the October 2024 Sonnet found simple jailbreaks and agent attacks defeating safeguards. That is a contemporaneous safeguard failure.
July 2024 paper, before the target window: testing gives no rigorous guarantee, and formal approaches are only proposed or restricted. This is consistent with the claim.

reviews.rationale: Independent pre-deployment testing in late 2024 showed a frontier model's safeguards failing under simple attacks. The packet shows no method that gave broad, independently scrutinised assurance of helpfulness, harmlessness and honesty. The research on formal approaches describes proposals or restricted guarantees, so it does not meet the contradiction condition.
